changes.local: If the bicycle in the preceding example had been on its wheels instead of upside-down, it would first have accelerated along the ground and then come to a stop. This connection between circular motion and linear motion needs to be explored. For example, it would be useful to know how linear and angular acceleration are related. In circular motion, linear acceleration is tangent to the circle at the point of interest, as seen in . Thus, linear acceleration is called tangential acceleration [MATH] . This is not to be confused with centripetal acceleration we covered earlier (see: ).
